reader.requirement: At --std 85, USAGE (DISPLAY implicit or explicit, BINARY, COMPUTATIONAL/COMP, PACKED-DECIMAL, INDEX) decides only the storage representation. Statements must give the same results for the same PICTURE and value whatever the usage: arithmetic, MOVE, compare, condition-names, subscripts, PERFORM VARYING, scaled and P-scaled items. The exception is a statement whose own rule restricts operand usage, such as ref-mod, STRING and INSPECT requiring DISPLAY at 85; those must be refused. The witness covers integer arithmetic, MOVE and compare across the five usages.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.Extension flags vendor spellings (COMP-1..COMP-5) only under the extension-flagging option; BINARY/COMP/COMPUTATIONAL/PACKED-DECIMAL/DISPLAY map to one Usage at every edition
post-1985 usages (NATIONAL, POINTER, BINARY-CHAR..DOUBLE, FLOAT-*, ...) refused COBOL0900 below their introducing edition
numeric item digit limit: 18 at COBOL-85, 31 at 2002+ (COBOL0802 for 19-31 at 85)

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition.|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry in Model/PicInfo.cs: none on ByteForm/StorageWidth/Truncation; ParseUsage reads the edition only through the nonstandard-extension flag.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the 1985 usages (gr2p stdout identical at 2023); yes for the set of usages: post-1985 usages are refused at 85 via VersionConformancePass#UsageConstructId
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf12_03 covers integer ADD/MOVE/compare/MULTIPLY/DIVIDE; it does not cover scaled/P-scaled items, unsigned receivers of a negative value, condition-names, subscripts and PERFORM VARYING on non-DISPLAY items, size error on packed, or the statement-restriction refusals

probes.printed: SCL=-012.34 x4 SEQ=YES PSC=YES 012300 ABS=0037 0037 C88=YES SUB=b V=e V=c V=a ACC=+00009 SBSIZE NEG=-999.99 -999.99 PSIZE PK=+99999
probes.expected: Scaled and P-scaled items agree across usages. Unsigned BINARY and PACKED receivers store the absolute value. Condition-names, subscripts and PERFORM VARYING on BINARY items work. Size error keeps the value for BINARY and PACKED.

probes.printed: error COBOL1647: reference modification of a numeric item of USAGE Binary ... is not permitted
probes.expected: §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.3 SR1 'Data-name-1 must reference a data item whose usage is DISPLAY' - refused

probes.printed: error COBOL1626 STRING sending operand 'NB' ... USAGE Binary; error COBOL1626 INSPECT identifier-1 'NB' ... USAGE Binary
probes.expected: the statements whose specifications restrict usage refuse a BINARY operand

probes.printed: COBOL0900 national data requires COBOL-2002; COBOL0900 USAGE POINTER requires COBOL-2002; COBOL0900 fixed-width binary usage requires COBOL-2002
probes.expected: usages the 1985 general format lacks are refused at 85
vendor usage spellings are an implementor extension. Accepting them is allowed, and ParseUsage flags them under the extension-flagging option.

reader.notes: Every usage feeds the same NumProfile arithmetic. Only ByteForm and StorageWidth differ by usage, and neither reads the edition. Statement-specific usage restrictions are enforced at 85. ACC=+00009 is the DISPLAY statement's implementor-defined rendering of a signed packed item, not a GR2 effect.

refuter.evidence: Attacked the 1985 statement restrictions the reader did not try and the uses that must NOT differ by usage. r2a: IF binary NUMERIC and IF packed NUMERIC refused COBOL6918 citing §1985:VI.6.3.1.2 (correct: 1985 requires DISPLAY). r2b-002: BINARY/PACKED integer compared with an alphanumeric literal refused COBOL2532; correct at 85 because cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.3.1.1.2 (6.3.1.1.2 Comparison of Nonnumeric Operands) 'Numeric and nonnumeric operands may be compared only when their usage is the same'. r2c: UNSTRING INTO a BINARY receiver refused COBOL1626 (cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR3). r2b-003 (EXIT 0): MOVE 9(4) BINARY/DISPLAY/PACKED to X(6) all [0042  ]; MOVE '0123' to BINARY and DISPLAY both 0123; BINARY and DISPLAY scaled to numeric-edited both [  12.50-]; DIVIDE GIVING REMAINDER identical (-014 -002) for BINARY and DISPLAY; COMPUTE ROUNDED identical (+03.3); UNSTRING with BINARY COUNT IN/POINTER and PACKED TALLYING works (AB CD 0002 0007 0002); STRING WITH POINTER on a COMP item accepted and works (06; STRING SR2 exempts identifier-4, cite.py: OK only as §1985:VI.6.25.3 SR2); INSPECT TALLYING into BINARY 0002; MOVE/ADD CORRESPONDING from DISPLAY to BINARY/PACKED members and INITIALIZE all correct. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.4 GR2  (5.14.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2. Side note only: the COBOL2532 and COBOL1626 refusals at --std 85 cite 2023 clauses, not the 1985 text (diagnostic citation, not a verdict defect).
